title: Quantum control as renormalization group flow
authors: Zuo Wang, Paul M. Schindler, Modesto Orozco-Ruiz, Nguyen H. Le, Florian Mintert, Marin Bukov
abstract: The Renormalization Group (RG) establishes relations between effective descriptions of physical systems at different scales; in Hamiltonian RG, these relations induce a flow in the space of Hamiltonians. In direct correspondence, we design an RG framework for quantum control by constructing a flow in the space of time-dependent Hamiltonians. A prescribed control subspace, selected to contain only experimentally accessible terms, forms the fixed-point manifold, while the flow preserves the target unitary and monotonically reduces the Hamiltonian weight outside this subspace. Exploiting the freedom in constructing the flow, we introduce flow-equation engineering to enhance the versatility of the framework for diverse control problems, including time-periodic and open-interval smooth protocols with prescribed endpoints. We provide two disparate applications to exhibit the utility of our approach: (i) Nonperturbative Floquet engineering beyond the regime of validity of high-frequency expansions, which we demonstrate by constructing an implementable time-periodic protocol for the Haldane model; (ii) Accessible fast-forward driving from unit-fidelity counterdiabatic evolution, which we showcase for large transverse-field Ising chains away from the adiabatic regime by compressing the long-range multibody adiabatic gauge potential into the original time-dependent Ising control schedules. Our control RG framework reveals a unifying perspective on Hamiltonian engineering and unitary quantum control, and can serve as an organizing principle behind seemingly disparate nonequilibrium quantum dynamics.
summary: This work introduces the Control Renormalization Group (CtrlsRG) framework, which maps quantum control design onto the mathematical structure of the Renormalization Group flow. By engineering this flow, the authors can systematically transform an ideal but inaccessible Hamiltonian into a physically implementable, accessible form. This offers a unifying principle for designing high-fidelity quantum gates and protocols.
main_problem: The paper develops a novel framework to design accessible quantum control protocols by structurally mapping the problem onto the Renormalization Group (RG) flow.
main_result: This Control RG (CtrlsRG) framework provides a unifying perspective on Hamiltonian engineering and unitary quantum control, successfully realizing protocols that surpass the accuracy of standard Floquet engineering methods.
method: The core method involves constructing a flow equation in the space of time-dependent Hamiltonians, parameterized by a flow variable $\mu$, which smoothly deforms an initially inaccessible Hamiltonian to an experimentally accessible fixed-point manifold while preserving the target unitary.
model_or_system: The framework applies to general quantum control problems governed by time-dependent Hamiltonians $H(t)$, demonstrated using models like the Haldane model and large transverse-field Ising chains.
key_observables: Target unitary fidelity ($F_\ell$), Hamiltonian weight outside the accessible subspace, and the flow parameter $\mu$.
important_parameters: Flow parameter $\mu$, drive frequency $\omega$, and system size $L$.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the existence of a flow that monotonically reduces the weight of inaccessible Hamiltonian terms while preserving the target unitary.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the RG flow in the Hamiltonian space, showing the transition from an initial state ($\mu=0$) to a final accessible state ($\mu 	o \infty$), and compare the infidelity of Floquet vs. CtrlsRG protocols.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the CtrlsRG concept by drawing an analogy to Hamiltonian RG, details the flow equation governing the Hamiltonian evolution, and validates the framework through two distinct applications: nonperturbative Floquet engineering and fast-forward driving.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, systematic, and theoretically grounded methodology (RG flow) to solve complex, non-adiabatic quantum control problems, which is highly relevant for designing experiments with trapped ions or superconducting qubits.
